rmi.lua.network_logic: Implements JRMP (Java Remote Method Protocol) and standard Java Object Serialization streams over TCP to coordinate method invokes against remote RMI services (like the RMI registry at port 1099 or JMX services).
rmi.lua.payload_raw: Wire handshake initiates with magic bytes 'JRMI' (0x4a524d49), 2 bytes version (2), and protocol byte (0x4b stream, 0x4c single-op, 0x4d multiplex). Server returns 0x4e ack followed by string host and int port. Call messages start with 0x50, stream magic (0xACED), stream version (0x0005), and block data/object tokens (e.g. TC_BLOCKDATA 0x77, TC_OBJECT 0x73, TC_CLASSDESC 0x72).
rmi.lua.edge_cases: Performs custom externalized serialization parsing (isExternalizable check) specifically targeting sun.rmi.server.UnicastRef / UnicastRef2 class formats to extract redirected endpoint definitions (e.g. @host:port); registers dynamic methods on JavaDOS/JavaDIS based on a JavaTypes layout map; tracks internal BufferedReader byte offsets to handle packet boundary fragmentation issues; skipCustomData recursively steps past nested serialization blocks until encountering TC_ENDBLOCKDATA (0x78) while keeping encountered class strings.

rsync.lua.network_logic: Implements client handshaking and modular directory list/queries for the Rsync protocol over TCP (typically port 873).
rsync.lua.payload_raw: Client initializes connection by sending version string like '@RSYNCD: 29\n'. Server returns similar version banner. Handshakes occur by exchanging plain-text command lines followed by newlines. Login response hashes passwords using MD4 ('\0\0\0\0' + password + challenge) encoded in Base64.
rsync.lua.edge_cases: Removes base64 padding suffix characters (the last 2 chars, typically '==') in login responses to comply with rsync's custom credential hashing scheme; verifies whether the module requires credentials by matching '@RSYNCD: AUTHREQD'; recursively reads module lists until meeting '@RSYNCD: EXIT'.

rtsp.lua.network_logic: Implements RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) request formatting, client socket wrapper, and response header decoding over TCP (typically port 554).
rtsp.lua.payload_raw:
Constructs standard RTSP plain-text requests: '<method> <url> RTSP/1.0
CSeq: <num>
<headers>

'. Parsers read server response banners matching '^RTSP%/1%.0 (%d*) ' followed by carriage return/line feed delimiters.
rtsp.lua.edge_cases: Ensures CSeq sequence numbers are incremented on every exchange and throws errors if missing; handles reconnection logic and socket retries automatically inside Client.exch if the remote host drops the connection; parses key-value header listings by iterating over carriage return boundaries split from the server response buffer.

functions: DigestMD5.new(self, chall, username, password, method, uri, service, realm)
sasl.lua.network_logic: Implements Simple Authentication and Security Layer (SASL) protocol helper wrappers, supporting PLAIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5, and NTLM v1 authentications across multiple application layer services (e.g. SMTP, IMAP, POP3, HTTP).
sasl.lua.payload_raw: PLAIN payload builds a null-separated string: '<authzid>\0<authcid>\0<passwd>'. CRAM-MD5 performs HMAC-MD5 on password/challenge. DIGEST-MD5 uses MD5 hashes to construct nested 'username/realm/nonce/cnonce/response' tokens. NTLM generates Type 3 responses from parsed Type 2 challenge flags using smbauth.
sasl.lua.edge_cases: Ensures parsing of challenge fields in DigestMD5.parseChallenge handles both double-quoted and raw values independently of spacing; matches target authentication flags NTLM_NegotiateExtendedSecurity (0x00080000) and NTLM_NegotiateUnicode (0x00000001) in NTLM messages to dynamically encode strings in UTF-16 representation via unicode.utf8to16; validates support boundaries for OpenSSL availability via HAVE_SSL flags.

shortport.lua.network_logic: Helper module to construct NSE portrule checks (e.g. portnumber, service name matching, version scan filters, and SSL/SSH detection queries).
shortport.lua.payload_raw: Maintains SSL handshake probe structures: TLSSessionReq client hello bytes, SSLSessionReq hello bytes, and DTLSSessionReq bytes to check for SSL/TLS features if nmap's engine-level service state is ambiguous.
shortport.lua.edge_cases: Validates parsed port range bounds (pstart <= pend, port numbers between 0 and 65535); caches active host-level SSL port scan states inside a locked host.registry.ssl table (via mutex locks) to prevent redundant probe exchanges; matches server response patterns to distinguish between SSL (e.g. '^\x16\x03') and non-SSL behaviors.

sip.lua.network_logic: Implements Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) client authentication, registration, options query, and INVITE sessions over UDP or TCP (typically port 5060).
sip.lua.payload_raw: Constructs standard SIP header text payloads separated by carriage returns/newlines. Invites construct standard Session Description Protocol (SDP) payloads describing IP4 audio options via rtpmap attributes.
sip.lua.edge_cases: Ensures authentication algorithms other than MD5 throw hard errors immediately; parses WWW-Authenticate or Proxy-Authenticate response headers and creates corresponding Digest authentication tokens; loops reading trying/ringing responses inside invite until an OK response code is received; supports custom timeout values specified by user script arguments.

slaxml.lua.network_logic: Pure-Lua SAX-like streaming XML parser used to parse structured XML response payloads from various services (e.g. SOAP, WebDAV, UPnP) without requiring external C libraries.
slaxml.lua.payload_raw: None directly. Processes raw XML string buffers using regex/string patterns: '^<%?([:%a_][:%w_.-]*) ?(.-)%?>' for processing instructions, '^<!%-%-(.-)%-%->' for comments, and '^<!%[CDATA%[(.-)%]%>' for CDATA chunks.
slaxml.lua.edge_cases: Unescapes XML entities via a lookup table for amp/lt/gt/quot/apos and uses unicode.utf8_enc for numeric character references like &#...;; manages nested namespace scopes (e.g. xmlns prefixes) using a dynamic lookup stack (nsStack) to resolve local attribute/element namespace URIs after their initial parsing; checks for well-formed state matching element open/close balance to warn on invalid nested DOM tags.

oops.lua.network_logic: Helper module to construct nested error message stacks for NSE library calls, providing clean debugging trace strings.
oops.lua.edge_cases: Implements `__tostring` returning different trace formatting based on nmap's runtime `debugging()` and `verbosity()` levels; `raise` wraps multi-value return parameters transparently (forwarding status and varargs) while wrapping the second parameter in an Oops stack if the status evaluates to false.

outlib.lua.network_logic: Helper module to format consistent, sorted output tables and comma-separated lists for NSE script reports.
outlib.lua.edge_cases: Overloads the Lua 5.2/5.3 `__pairs` metamethod inside sorted_by_key to return a custom coroutine wrap/yield generator that yields keys in sorted order using table.sort; modifies existing object metatables inline in list_sep without overwriting non-target functions.

rpcap.lua.network_logic: Implements the WinPcap Remote Capture (rpcap) protocol for authenticating to remote sniffers and discovering local networking interfaces over TCP (port 2002).
rpcap.lua.payload_raw: Generates big-endian binary packets. Request header is: '>BBI2I4' (version=0, message type, value, payload length). Authentication options write '>I2I2I2I2' (auth type: 1=PWD, 0=NULL; dummy; length of username; length of password) followed by raw username and password strings.
rpcap.lua.edge_cases: FindAllInterfaces.parse reads individual addresses, evaluating family codes to distinguish between IPv4 (0x0002) and IPv6 (0x0017) formats; automatically constructs CIDR representation for interfaces returning non-null netmask values via ipOps.subnet_to_cidr; registers packet types 1 (Error), 130 (FindAllInterfaces), and 136 (Authentication) to direct parsing handlers.

smb2.lua.network_logic: Implements Server Message Block (SMB) version 2 and 3 negotiation protocol, handling SMB dialects from 2.0.2 up to 3.1.1 over TCP (typically port 445).
smb2.lua.payload_raw: Encodes SMB2 headers using little-endian packs: '<c4 I2 I2 I4 I2 I2 I4 I4 I8 I4 I4 I8 c16' representing ProtocolId ('\xFESMB'), StructureSize (64), CreditCharge, Status, Command, CreditRequest, Flags, NextCommand, MessageId, Reserved, TreeId, SessionId, and Signature. Dialect lists and context headers (e.g. preauth/encryption contexts) are appended after padding fields to align contexts.
smb2.lua.edge_cases: Aligns NegotiateContext blocks in SMB 3.1.1 packets by inserting zero-byte padding strings matching `(8 - total_data % 8) % 8`; handles Unix-to-NT time conversions for server_time and start_time via `(time // 10000000) - 11644473600`; handles NetBIOS framing header parsing (length extraction from first 4 bytes using `length & 0x00FFFFFF`).

smtp.lua.network_logic: Implements Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) client functionality, including command exchange, verification, STARTTLS session wrapping, and SASL authentication on SMTP ports (typically 25, 465, 587).
smtp.lua.payload_raw:
Sends text commands ending with '
'. Multi-line data inputs end with '
.
'. Authentication values (such as auth payloads and credentials) are base64-encoded via the base64 library prior to transmission.
smtp.lua.edge_cases: Evaluates response codes mapping to success definitions inside `SMTP_CMD` lookup table (e.g. EHLO success code is 250, STARTTLS ready code is 220); parses authentication capability fields in EHLO output using match pattern `'%d+%-AUTH%s(.*)$'` splitting by spaces; supports LOGIN, PLAIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5, and NTLM (using hardcoded NTLMSSP challenge strings) via SASL helpers.

snmp.lua.network_logic: Implements Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) version 1 and 2c queries and Trap encapsulation over UDP (typically port 161).
snmp.lua.payload_raw: Encodes SNMP PDUs into ASN.1 Basic Encoding Rules (BER). Defines custom tag encoders for table types mapping to OIDs ('\x06'), IP addresses ('\x40'), counters/gauges/timeticks ('\x41', '\x42', '\x43', '\x44'). Context tags: GetRequest ('\xa0'), GetNextRequest ('\xa1'), Response-PDU ('\xa2'), SetRequest ('\xa3'), Trap ('\xa4'), GetBulkRequest ('\xa5').
snmp.lua.edge_cases: Extracts creds credentials (VALID/PARAM states) automatically if community string is not supplied; parses nested ASN.1 sequence results via fetchResponseValues to map BER octets back to dotted-decimal IPv4 address strings for IP tags ('\x40'); retries packet sends up to `snmp.retries` times upon timeout before returning failure.

socks.lua.network_logic: Implements the SOCKS version 5 proxy protocol client interface, establishing TCP socket connections and handling authentication handshakes.
socks.lua.payload_raw: Sends version/method negotiations packed as: 'Bs1' (socks version 5 followed by method codes string). Credentials are sent as 'Bs1s1' (sub-negotiation version 1 followed by username and password length-prefixed strings). Responses are received as 2-byte buffers unpacked via 'BB'.
socks.lua.edge_cases: Coerces single authentication method integers to single-element tables inside Request.Connect; replaces empty username/password strings with single null byte strings ('\0') during packaging to satisfy SOCKS protocol length specs; handles 0xFF response method signifying no acceptable authentication mechanisms.

srvloc.lua.network_logic: Implements the Service Location Protocol (SLP / srvloc) version 2 for discovering services and network attributes over UDP multicast (port 427). Defaults to multicast group IPv4 239.255.255.253 or IPv6 FF02::116.
srvloc.lua.payload_raw: Generates big-endian network packets. Request.Service serializes as: '>BBI3I2I3I2s2I2s2s2I2I2' (version, function, total packet length, flags, next extension offset, xid, language tag string, prev response list length, service type string, scope string, predicate length, SLP SPI length). Response headers unpack with: '>BBI3I2' (version, func, len, flags) followed by (>I3I2s2) for next extension, xid, lang tag.
srvloc.lua.edge_cases: Unpacks 24-bit length parameters ('I3') for overall packet size and next extension offset; loops on ServiceRequest socket reads until no response is returned to gather all responding hosts (multicast responses); increments transaction ID (xid) after each command transaction.

ssh1.lua.network_logic: Implements basic SSH-1 client handshake and public key retrieval (RSA1) over TCP (port 22). Key verification matches against locally parsed known_hosts files.
ssh1.lua.payload_raw: Exchanges standard banners ending in '\r\n' (e.g. sends 'SSH-1.5-Nmap-SSH1-Hostkey\r\n'). Packages SSH-1 binary packets with payload length header '>I4' followed by padding matching `8 - payload_length % 8` bytes.
ssh1.lua.edge_cases: Calculates bubble babble phonetic representations using custom consonant/vowel maps and a modular checksum seed value; produces OpenSSH-style 17x9 ASCII visual art ('drunken bishop' random walk) from fingerprint bytes; parses ~/.ssh/config and UserKnownHostsFile parameters to locate alternate known_hosts files.

ssh2.lua.network_logic: Implements the SSH-2 transport layer protocol, handling Diffie-Hellman key exchanges (group1, group14, group16, and group-exchange variants) and key retrieval (DSA, RSA, ECDSA, ED25519) over TCP (port 22).
ssh2.lua.payload_raw: Generates big-endian network packets. Headers write: '>I4B' (packet length, padding length). Bignums are packed via `pack_mpint` prepended by big-endian 4-byte lengths. Standard `kex_init` options encode standard cryptographic algorithm lists with string packs: '>s4s4 s4s4 s4s4 s4s4 s4s4 BI4'.
ssh2.lua.edge_cases: Ensures that packet padding lengths are at least 4 bytes and pad out the total packet size to a multiple of 8; handles mpint packaging by prepending a null byte string ('\0') if the bignum's most significant bit is set (avoiding interpretation as a negative number in two's complement); supports Oakley Groups 2, 14, and 16 primes for modular exponentiation calculations via openssl bignum operations.

sslv2.lua.network_logic: Implements binary communications for the SSLv2 protocol, enabling client hellos, key exchanges, and supported cipher suite queries over TLS/SSL ports (typically port 443).
sslv2.lua.payload_raw: Encodes SSLv2 record headers as: big-endian '>I2' with the most significant bit set (`length | 0x8000`) for 2-byte header records (no padding), or '>I2B' for 3-byte header records (containing a padding length byte). Hello payloads package version and length specifications as '>BI2I2I2I2' (MSG-CLIENT-HELLO=1, version=2, cipher spec length, session ID length, challenge length).
sslv2.lua.edge_cases: Extracts record lengths by masking off header MSB tags (`len & 0x7fff` for 2-byte headers, `len & 0x3fff` for 3-byte headers); reads incomplete buffers on-the-fly via `read_atleast` looping socket receives until requested byte lengths are satisfied; handles STARTTLS session preparation inline before sending raw SSLv2 hellos.

strbuf.lua.network_logic: Helper module implementing a mutable string buffer to avoid inefficient Lua string copies during sequential string concatenations (e.g. assembling HTTP/binary payloads).
strbuf.lua.edge_cases: Overloads the concatenation `__concat`, comparison `__eq`, and string conversion `__tostring` metamethods; requires the left-hand operand of `..` to be the string buffer instance; defaults the `__tostring` separator to a newline ('\n') but allows raw concatenation using `strbuf.dump(buf, delimiter)`. Clones sub-buffers recursively when appending one buffer into another.

strict.lua.network_logic: Development sanity checking helper that enforces runtime global variable declarations inside Lua script environments to prevent accidental global scope pollution.
strict.lua.edge_cases: Overloads target environment's `__index` and `__newindex` metamethods; uses `debug.getinfo(3, 'S')` to inspect call-stack provenance (identifying if reads/writes originate from 'main' script scope, nested function scopes, or compiled 'C' closures); raises explicit Lua interpreter errors when indexing or assigning to vars not logged in the local environment's `__declared` tracker.

stringaux.lua.network_logic: Helper module providing common utility functions for string formatting, parsing, splitting, escaping, and pattern matching inside NSE scripts.
stringaux.lua.edge_cases: Enforces non-empty delimiters in `strsplit` to prevent infinite loops; handles dot-directories ('.' and '..') explicitly inside `filename_escape` by encoding them to '%2e' and '%2e%2e' respectively; tracks nested bracket state via `in_brackets` flag inside `ipattern` to avoid wrapping characters already inside a character class (e.g. `[a-z]`) with duplicate brackets.

stun.lua.network_logic: Implements Session Traversal Utilities for NAT (STUN) protocol client operations, allowing binding requests to discover NAT mappings, public IP addresses, and STUN server version tags over UDP (typically port 3478). Supports both Classic (RFC3489) and Modern (RFC5389) transaction modes.
stun.lua.payload_raw: Generates big-endian network packets. Headers write as: '>I2I2' (type, length) followed by a 16-byte transaction ID (trans_id). Attributes serialize as '>I2I2' (type, length) followed by value bytes. Address attributes are unpacked using: '>xBI2c4' (family, port, IPv4 address).
stun.lua.edge_cases: Differentiates Classic and Modern STUN protocol modes by formatting the transaction ID: Classic uses 16 random bytes, while Modern prepends a 4-byte Magic Cookie ('\x21\x12\xA4\x42') followed by 12 random bytes; processes variable-length STUN response loops by parsing header-specified packet length values; maps STUN attributes dynamically including source, changed, mapped, and response addresses.

tab.lua.network_logic: Helper formatting module designed to arrange script console outputs into structured columns and aligned text tables (reminiscent of Nmap's C++ NmapOutputTable implementation).
tab.lua.edge_cases: Calculates column alignments dynamically inside `dump` by measuring the maximum length string in each column position; appends an additional two spaces ('  ') of pad spacing between columns; skips padding the final element of a row; handles missing intermediate columns safely by inserting empty strings.

target.lua.network_logic: Helper module for adding newly discovered target IPs or hostnames to the current Nmap engine scan queue at runtime.
target.lua.edge_cases: Requires the user to pass the `newtargets` script argument to enable `ALLOW_NEW_TARGETS`; respects the `max-newtargets` parameter ceiling (where 0 or nil indicates no limit) by querying `nmap.new_targets_num()` and tracking pushed target tallies; rejects additions from postrule scripts (only prerule, portrule, and hostrule scripts are permitted targets insertion privileges).

tftp.lua.network_logic: Implements a mini, write-only TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) server running over UDP port 69, allowing Nmap scripts to receive files uploaded by remote target hosts.
tftp.lua.payload_raw: TFTP binary packets package OpCodes, block counts, and data. ACK formats: big-endian '>I2I2' (OpCode.ACK=4, block number). ERROR formats: '>I2I2z' (OpCode.ERROR=5, error code, null-terminated message string). WRQ (write request) parses string: '>I2' (OpCode.WRQ=2) followed by double null-terminated strings for filename and encoding type ('zz'). DATA packets parse '>I2I2' (OpCode.DATA=3, block number) followed by block byte payload.
tftp.lua.edge_cases: Manages socket threading multiplexing using Lua coroutines inside a centralized `dispatcher` handler; validates block order sequential integrity (asserts first block is #1 and cross-checks every 5 blocks for missing segments); closes socket connection when receiving a block size under 512 bytes (marking EOF); uses `nmap.condvar` signal variables to synchronize file search loops.

tls.lua.network_logic: Encapsulates full SSL/TLS and DTLS record layer formatting, message parsing, and handshake logic. Supports constructing customizable ClientHello handshakes, reading/buffering SSL/TLS records from network sockets, and parsing ServerHello, ServerKeyExchange parameters, and TLS certificates.
tls.lua.payload_raw: Constructs TLS records with a 5-byte header pack('>B I2 I2', ContentType, Version, Length). Generates client random bytes composed of epoch timestamp (pack('>I4', os.time())) and 28 bytes of entropy. Handshake messages are packed as pack('B>I3', HandshakeType, Length) followed by body. Parses DH params with pack('>s2s2s2', p, g, y) and SRP parameters with pack('>s2s2s1s2', N, g, s, B). Identifies HelloRetryRequest by verifying if server random bytes match the specific 32-byte SHA-256 hash of 'HelloRetryRequest'.
tls.lua.edge_cases: Tracks TLSv1.3 version upgrade logic where a TLSv1.2 ServerHello with a supported_versions extension of '\x03\x04' is dynamically promoted to TLSv1.3; supports parsing of RFC 8998 ShangMi ciphers by checking curveSM2 curves and sm2sig_sm3 signature schemes; handles record-level fragmentation by storing leftover payload fragments across socket buffer reads; calculates RSA-equivalence strength for various keys using NIST SP800-57 Part 1 recommendations.

tableaux.lua.network_logic: None. This is an auxiliary utility library that provides basic table data-structure helper operations for other NSE libraries.
tableaux.lua.payload_raw: None. The module does not perform network operations or generate binary/text transmission payloads.
tableaux.lua.edge_cases: Performs deep table copies (`tcopy`) and shallow copies (`shallow_tcopy`) using `next` instead of standard `pairs` to ensure raw key/value traversal bypassing any active metatables. Allows restricting searches using standard array iteration (`ipairs`) instead of full key-value space traversal (`pairs`) in the `contains` utility.

tn3270.lua.network_logic: Implements an RFC 1576 and 2355 compliant TN3270/TN3270E Telnet client emulator. Negotiates connection options (Binary Transmission, End of Record, Terminal Type, TN3270, TN3270E) using standard Telnet command codes and handles screen buffer updating over TCP or SSL.
tn3270.lua.payload_raw: Telnet options are negotiated via IAC sequences (e.g., WILL/WONT/DO/DONT option codes). Data streams are framed using IAC EOR ('\xff\xef') at the end of the packet. Attention Identifiers (AID) include ENTER ('\x7d'), CLEAR ('\x6d'), and PF keys. TN3270E packets prefix payload with a 5-byte headers (e.g. '\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00'). Transmits EBCDIC encoded characters for user inputs via drda.StringUtil.toEBCDIC.
tn3270.lua.edge_cases: Performs custom 12-bit vs 14-bit buffer address decoding depending on the most significant bits of the first address byte; escapes all raw '\xff' bytes in the output data streams by doubling them to '\xff\xff' to avoid colliding with Telnet command parsers; tracks screen attributes (fa_buffer) to scan for hidden credential fields or writeable cursor boundaries.

tns.lua.network_logic: Provides a client implementation of the Oracle Transparent Network Substrate (TNS) protocol. It manages transport-level connection initiation, SNS security handshake, OS and protocol negotiations, session authentication, Listener Control command execution, SQL query processing, and server-side response parsing for Oracle 10g and 11g database servers.
tns.lua.payload_raw: TNS frames prefix payloads with an 8-byte header pack('>I2I2BBI2', Length, Checksum, Type, Reserved, HeaderChecksum). Packet types are CONNECT(1), ACCEPT(2), REFUSE(4), DATA(6), and MARKER(12). PreAuth/Auth payloads serialize fields into Key-Value Pairs (KVPs) using custom length-value structures. Initiates connection via standard connection descriptors like '(DESCRIPTION=(ADDRESS=...))' or command strings like '(COMMAND=status)'.
tns.lua.edge_cases: Implements complex cryptographic handshakes: Oracle 10g password hashing via DES-CBC and session key decryption via AES-128-CBC; Oracle 11g session key derivation using SHA1 and AES-192-CBC; parses Oracle-specific internal DataTypes such as NUMBER (evaluating bitwise sign flags to offset base-100 mantissas) and DATE (restoring year/month values using byte-offset schemas).

unicode.lua.network_logic: Helper library for handling string transformations, character conversions, and character encoding detection. Does not initiate raw network sockets but supports packet decoding/encoding tasks for other application protocols (such as SMB/Windows domain strings).
unicode.lua.payload_raw: Not applicable. Acts purely as a local parser/transformer of character buffers into various Unicode (UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE, ASCII) or Windows OEM (Code Page 437) formats.
unicode.lua.edge_cases: Performs byte-order mark (BOM) sniffing to identify UTF-16LE ('\xff\xfe'), UTF-16BE ('\xfe\xff'), or UTF-8 ('\xef\xbb\xbf') headers; determines endianness by relative position of null bytes when no BOM is present; falls back to 'other' classification for binary or unrecognized 8-bit encodings.

unittest.lua.network_logic: Testing harness framework library for verifying the behavior of other NSE libraries. It contains no network socket logic or transport-layer protocols.
unittest.lua.payload_raw: Not applicable. Handles pure unit-testing logic internally.
unittest.lua.edge_cases: Dynamically inspects imported library packages for the presence of the global 'test_suite' variable to execute their nested tests; implements recursive identical check ('identical') that deep-compares tables (by size, type, keys, and values) to verify complex structural equivalence.

unpwdb.lua.network_logic: Helper database utility library for reading and iterating over username and password dictionaries used in brute-forcing scripts. Does not contain active network communication code.
unpwdb.lua.payload_raw: Not applicable. Interacts with local database files 'nselib/data/usernames.lst' and 'nselib/data/passwords.lst'.
unpwdb.lua.edge_cases: Enforces strict timing thresholds (T0-T5 templates) and maximum iteration limit filters (unpwdb.userlimit / unpwdb.passlimit / unpwdb.timelimit) to auto-terminate brute force runs on slow services; skips comment prefix markers ('#!comment:') during database compilation; provides a 'reset' signal to restart nested loops.

upnp.lua.network_logic: Handles UPnP (Universal Plug and Play) and SSDP (Simple Service Discovery Protocol) queries over UDP port 1900. It supports sending M-SEARCH multicast discovery queries, receiving UDP replies, and retrieving detailed device descriptions via HTTP GET requests.
upnp.lua.payload_raw:
SSDP queries transmit standard HTTP-like packets over UDP: 'M-SEARCH * HTTP/1.1
Host:239.255.255.250:1900
ST:upnp:rootdevice
Man:"ssdp:discover"
MX:3

'. Parser parses SSDP responses containing headers: USN (Unique Service Name), Location (XML URL), and Server.
upnp.lua.edge_cases: Handles IPv4 multicast ('239.255.255.250') vs IPv6 Link-Local multicast ('FF02::C') endpoints; provides target location overrides to ensure retrieval of XML files from scanned target IPs when the device returns a mismatched internal host address; parses hierarchical XML files using SAX event-driven handlers (slaxml) to isolate devices and services under UDN (Unique Device Name) keys.

url.lua.network_logic: Helper utility library for URL routing, path resolution, and URI parsing. It contains no active socket communication code.
url.lua.payload_raw: Not applicable. Locally parses and reformats URL target strings, query parameters, and relative paths.
url.lua.edge_cases: Resolves IDN hostnames (containing UTF-8/non-ASCII characters) into Punycode ACE format using idna/unicode; resolves relative URL paths (handling '.' and '..') following RFC 3986 path merging rules; automatically decodes HTML entity strings like '&', '<', and '>' during query parameter parsing.

versant.lua.network_logic: Implements the administrative communication protocol for the Versant Object Database. Sends padded command blocks (2048 bytes) over TCP, retrieves database lists/ports, and interacts with the dynamically allocated Object Database Engine (OBE) port.
versant.lua.payload_raw: Admin commands prefix payloads with hardcoded hex structures (e.g. '00010000000000000002...') and pack null-terminated command strings, usernames, and database versions, padding to 2048 bytes. OBE requests send control packets starting with '1002005d00000000000100000000000d000000000000000000000000' followed by options like '-noprint -i ', padded to 256 bytes.
versant.lua.edge_cases: Aligns the command string buffer to even 4-byte boundaries before appending headers; handles multi-stage socket reads (getNodeInfo reads database count, buffer size, then loops over records to read fixed-offset fields for name, owner, created, and version); parses dynamically returned TCP ports (big-endian 16-bit or 32-bit values) to map subsequent database listener targets.

vnc.lua.network_logic: Implements client-side RFB (Remote Framebuffer) protocol for VNC administration and authentication. Supports standard version handshakes, security type negotiation, and multi-layered authentication wrappers including TLS/SSL tunnels.
vnc.lua.payload_raw: Negotiates version string (e.g. 'RFB 003.008\n'). Sends chosen security type bytes. Standard VNCAuth transmits the 16-byte response encrypted under a bit-reversed key. TightVNC/VeNCrypt send subtype numbers and tunnels. Apple Remote Desktop uses DH key exchange followed by username/password blobs encrypted via AES-128-ECB.
vnc.lua.edge_cases: Performs custom VNC DES key preparation where the password is truncated or padded with nulls to 8 bytes, and each byte has its bits reversed using bit-shifting operations; handles ATEN iKVM variants which send 24-byte packets directly during Tight negotiation; implements Diffie-Hellman key exchange for Apple Remote Desktop (security type 30) using big numbers (openssl.bignum) and MD5/AES-128-ECB cryptography.

vulns.lua.network_logic: No active network scanning. Provides a standardized reporting framework to capture, structure, and format detected vulnerabilities inside Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE) scripts.
vulns.lua.payload_raw: Not applicable. Interacts with memory reports and structured tables.
vulns.lua.edge_cases: Filters vulnerability display based on user arguments like 'vulns.show-all' or 'vulns.short'; formats reference URLs using popular vulnerability IDs (CVE, OSVDB, BID) via registered hook callbacks; manages threat states (NOT_VULN, LIKELY_VULN, VULN, DoS, EXPLOIT) with customizable description fields, check results, and exploit proof logs.

vuzedht.lua.network_logic: Implements the Vuze Distributed Hash Table (DHT) client protocol over UDP. Supports connecting to DHT nodes, generating session-tracked transaction IDs, sending PING and FIND_NODE requests, and parsing binary response structures.
vuzedht.lua.payload_raw: Constructs binary packets starting with connection IDs prefixing big-endian packed headers containing action codes, transaction IDs, protocol versions, network IDs, local IP address strings (length-prefixed), port numbers, instance IDs, and timestamps. FIND_NODE appends a node ID ('\xA7' + 19 random bytes), status (0xFFFFFFFF), and DHT size.
vuzedht.lua.edge_cases: Encodes transaction headers using random 8-character connection IDs prefixed with a hardcoded '\xFF' byte; extracts and converts local socket binding details dynamically using socket:get_info() to populate correct external-facing IP/port session headers; parses nested multi-contact response lists where each entry is packed as a byte-length-prefixed binary string representing IPv4/IPv6 address blocks and big-endian 16-bit ports; handles error action redirects (type 1) indicating 'wrong address' redirect targets.

wsdd.lua.network_logic: Implements Web Service Dynamic Discovery (WSDD / WS-Discovery) probes over UDP port 3702. Supports unicast and multicast targeting (using IPv4 239.255.255.250 or IPv6 FF02::C). It generates SOAP envelope messages and tracks received SOAP response XML blocks.
wsdd.lua.payload_raw: Transmits XML-formatted SOAP envelopes containing Probe requests. Probe payloads request target service types using addressing headers (MessageID, To, Action). Includes placeholders like '#uuid#' which are dynamically substituted with random GUIDs.
wsdd.lua.edge_cases: Requires OpenSSL (openssl.rand_bytes) to generate valid UUIDs for SOAP message header tracking; extracts nested XML elements using non-greedy pattern matching (SOAP-ENV:Reason/Text, MessageID, XAddrs, Types) instead of parsing the entire DOM; automatically adds discovered hosts to Nmap target lists using target.add() if ALLOW_NEW_TARGETS is active; eliminates duplicate packets using a global message ID registry table.

xdmcp.lua.payload_raw: Encapsulates binary packets with a 6-byte big-endian header (2-byte version, 2-byte opcode, 2-byte payload length) followed by protocol fields such as length-prefixed strings, array structures of client IP addresses and connection type fields.

xmpp.lua.network_logic: Implements a subset of the Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP / Jabber) over TCP (typically port 5222 or 5269). Performs XML stream handshakes, negotiates STARTTLS upgrades, parses stream features, and executes multi-mechanism SASL authentication.
xmpp.lua.payload_raw: Initiates streams using standard XML elements ('<?xml...><stream:stream...>') and transmits SASL handshake nodes ('<auth mechanism=...>', '<response>').
xmpp.lua.edge_cases: Implements socket-drain rules inside XMPP:send() by setting socket timeout to 1ms to flush trailing unread buffer bytes; parses raw XML elements using string.find/gmatch regular expressions (Vasiliy Kulikov's parser) without a full XML parser library; supports dynamic SSL socket upgrading via socket:reconnect_ssl() when negotiating STARTTLS; executes complex multi-step handshakes for SASL authentication mechanisms including PLAIN, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5, and DIGEST-MD5.

http.lua.payload_raw: Constructs standard HTTP requests formatted with method, URI, headers, host details, content-length, cookies, and raw post data. Emits CR-LF terminated request streams.
http.lua.edge_cases: Implements extensive 404 detection logic (identify_404) that tests lower/upper case filenames and non-existent directories to dynamically deduce whether the target uses standard 404 codes, soft 200 codes, or distinct custom bodies; caches HTTP response attributes in host.registry to prevent repeated scans; decodes stacked content-encodings like gzip/deflate; parses HTML form parameters and inputs (grab_forms, parse_form) via regex; manages NTLMv2 auth handshakes by calling into smbauth.lua.

nmap.luadoc.network_logic: Core C-level binding interface inside the Nmap engine. Offers direct wrappers for socket I/O (TCP, UDP, SSL/TLS) via Nsock, raw packet capture via libpcap (Berkeley Packet Filters), raw frame/packet injection via libdnet (dnet), and target metadata queries (ports, timing, interfaces).
nmap.luadoc.payload_raw: Used to send/receive raw TCP/UDP streams, raw Ethernet frames (ethernet_send), or raw IP packets (ip_send).
nmap.luadoc.edge_cases: Manages connection timeouts, thread synchronization mutexes and condition variables (mutex, condvar) for script parallelism; provides non-blocking socket emulation; retrieves peer SSL certificate details (get_ssl_certificate) including validity ranges and parsed public key parameters; handles custom IP packet creation by requiring exact target scope identifiers in IPv6 environments.

openssl.luadoc.network_logic: No active network scanning. Exposes OpenSSL cryptographic routines for cipher block encryption/decryption, HMAC signature calculation, message digests (SHA, MD5, RIPEMD), and arbitrary-precision big number arithmetic (bignum).
openssl.luadoc.payload_raw: Not applicable. Interacts with memory strings and big numbers.
openssl.luadoc.edge_cases: Implements Miller-Rabin probabilistic primality checks (bignum_is_prime, bignum_is_safe_prime) with a default confidence level bounds (false positive rate < 2^-80); enforces strict initialization vector and key constraints during cipher selection (encrypt, decrypt); converts 56-bit DES keys into odd-parity corrected 64-bit keys (DES_string_to_key); checks PRNG seed entropy availability when creating cryptographically strong random blocks (rand_bytes).

rpc.lua.network_logic: Performs RPC (Remote Procedure Call) operations over UDP or TCP, communicating with portmapper (rpcbind) on port 111, mountd, and NFS services. Supports RPC versions 1 through 3, NULL or UNIX authentication, and queries endpoints dynamically mapping RPC program names to numbers.
rpc.lua.payload_raw: Encodes RPC transaction headers (XID, call types, unix/null verifiers) and RPC message fields (opaque/vopaque/integer payloads) aligned to 4-byte boundaries (CalcFillBytes). Runs raw socket writes/reads via Comm:SendPacket and Comm:ReceivePacket.
rpc.lua.edge_cases: Performs source-port binding redirection within 512-1023 range on privileged environments to comply with secure RPC source port checks; caches remote portmapper table lookups inside nmap.registry; corrects NetApp NULL-padding anomalies on version 3 protocol queries; handles socket fragment reassembly for RPC-over-TCP streams (ReceivePacket).

smb.lua.network_logic: Implements the SMB (Server Message Block) version 1 protocol over NetBIOS (ports 137, 139) or raw TCP (port 445). Establishes connections, negotiates dialects, starts authentication sessions, connects to IPC$ or disk trees, handles file read/write operations, and searches files/directories on shares.
smb.lua.payload_raw: Constructs raw SMB v1 command packets with standardized SMB headers (command codes, security signatures via MD5 message_sign, target tree IDs TID, process IDs PID, user IDs UID, multiplex IDs MID). Connects via standard Nmap sockets.
smb.lua.edge_cases: Handles connection overrides (custom credentials/pass hashes/LM/NTLM encryption); manages NetBIOS host/session negotiation sequences; processes multi-packet SMB transaction reassembly (receive_transaction2); buffers NT_STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW responses during named pipe reads by issuing iterative follow-up reads.

stdnse.lua.network_logic: Standard utility library. Does not directly initiate network sockets or scanning traffic, but assists in managing socket read buffers (make_buffer/lines) and host timeouts.
stdnse.lua.edge_cases: Manages registry namespaces for shared state data across scripts; parses complex time unit suffixes (s, m, h, ms) inside parse_timespec; provides fallbacks for retrieving command line script arguments via nmap.registry.

sslcert.lua.network_logic: Performs SSL/TLS socket connections (via wrap_close, wrap_receive, wrap_send socket hooks), handles STARTTLS protocol negotiation wrapper checks for multiple application protocols (FTP, IMAP, LDAP, LMTP, MySQL, NNTP, POP3, PostgreSQL, SMTP, TDS, VNC, XMPP), and fetches SSL certificates from targets.
sslcert.lua.payload_raw: Wraps raw app-level STARTTLS protocol negotiation payloads (e.g. SMTP 'STARTTLS', FTP 'AUTH TLS', XMPP '<starttls xmlns=...', VNC security negotiations) before upgrading the connection to SSL/TLS via nse ssl upgrade.
sslcert.lua.edge_cases: Caches fetched certificates inside host/port registries to prevent redundant network handshake requests; supports fallback socket reconnection for legacy servers not handling in-place starttls connection upgrades; parses raw DER-encoded certificate structures to extract validation limits, issuer DN fields, and cryptographic public keys.

smbauth.lua.network_logic: Helper cryptographic library for SMB. Does not perform socket logic directly, but compiles and processes credentials, security tokens (security_blob), and computes cryptographic response signatures (LM, NTLM, NTLMv2, LMv2, NTLMv2 session response) sent to SMB servers.
smbauth.lua.payload_raw: Encodes security tokens, SPNEGO/NTLMSSP challenge responses, cryptographic hashes (DES, MD4, MD5, HMAC-MD5), and message signatures (MAC keys) compiled into SMB session setup payloads.
smbauth.lua.edge_cases: Computes password hashes from standard plaintext or pre-computed password hash strings; handles extended security negotiation flags (is_extended) using NTLM SSP; extracts system attributes (DNS hostname, domain name, OS version) directly out of GSS-API/SPNEGO security blobs (get_host_info_from_security_blob).
